title: Multimodal Early Detection of Anthracycline-Induced Cardiotoxicity Using Layer-Specific Strain Analysis
summary: Certain cancer medications can damage the heart. This study investigates whether a new cardiac MRI analysis method (layer-specific strain analysis) can detect such damage earlier than the usual measurement of pumping function by cardiac ultrasound. 120 cancer patients will be examined before, during and after chemotherapy.
conditions: Cardiomyopathy due to drugs and other external agents

interventions.name: Patients scheduled for anthracycline-based chemotherapy undergo serial cardiac imaging at 4 timepoints: baseline, after cycle 4, 4 weeks post-chemotherapy, and 6 months post-treatment. Each assessment includes contrast-enhanced cardiac MRI with layer-specific strain analysis (feature tracking) and T

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned anthracycline-based chemotherapy (doxorubicin, epirubicin, daunorubicin); baseline LVEF ≥50%; written informed consent; no contraindications to MRI
Exclusion criteria:
Pre-existing cardiomyopathy or LVEF <50%; severe cardiac arrhythmias; renal insufficiency (eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73 m²); pregnancy/breastfeeding; prior anthracycline exposure; severe valvular disease; claustrophobia or MRI contraindications; prior chest radiation >30 Gy; severe psychiatric disease; participation in other studies with medicinal products
